purpose: Test whether ranking appendix grasp handles by swept URDF collision-mesh clearance avoids the observed left jaw/cecum inversion.

method.geometry: URDF collision meshes for the instrument links, represented by up to 2048 vertex/face-centroid samples per link
method.obstacle: current deformed cecum FEM boundary vertices
method.trajectory: tip-to-standoff-to-handle path sampled every 5 mm; sampled instrument orientation follows the trocar-to-tip axis
method.scope: scripted DemoPolicy only; Newton contact solver remains authoritative; all material and tissue parameters unchanged

comparisons.mode: existing endpoint-clearance selection, target recomputed each control step
swept-mesh clearance with target reselected each control step
comparisons.interpretation: This version was worse; dynamic target reselection is rejected.

comparisons.mode: swept-mesh clearance with target locked for the approach
comparisons.trajectory_comparison: Tip poses and actions were exactly identical to the endpoint-clearance run for all 24 recorded steps.
comparisons.interpretation: The geometric ranking selected the same target and did not improve the outcome.

comparisons.trajectory_comparison: Tip poses and actions were exactly identical to the baseline run.

decision: Keep --demo-swept-clearance opt-in and disabled by default. The current proxy does not establish safe contact or help this held start condition; a better mesh-distance/trajectory model and held-out starts are needed before promotion.
limitations: Vertex and face-centroid samples are only an approximation to continuous mesh-to-surface distance.
This one deterministic scripted seed is not an RL, held-out anatomy, or statistical evaluation.
Contact force remains uncalibrated against physical tissue or an instrumented phantom.
privacy: All runs and geometry processing were local; no personal data or raw videos are included in this record.
